45	THE PLAN:
46	# Muxy vs Workroom test practices — findings
47	
48	## Context
49	
50	Joel asked for a review of how Muxy (`~/dev/muxy`, sibling ghostty-based Swift terminal app,
51	pulled to latest `origin/main` @ `03a6420`, 2026-08-12) implements its tests, to see what could
52	improve Workroom's macapp test suite. This is a findings-only writeup — no code changes.
53	
54	Both projects are macOS/SwiftUI apps built on libghostty with git/VCS-heavy domains, which makes
55	the comparison unusually direct. Key framework difference up front: **Muxy is 100% Swift Testing
56	(`@Test`/`#expect`, 334 files, 3,297 tests); Workroom is 100% XCTest (147 files, 2,263 tests).**
57	No Swift Testing migration is proposed — at Workroom's scale that's a non-starter, and several
58	Muxy patterns below are trait-shaped (`.serialized`, `.timeLimit`, `@Test(arguments:)`) with no
59	clean XCTest equivalent, so they're named as XCTest-form translations or dropped, not copied.
60	
61	## Adoptable patterns, ranked
62	
63	### 1. Actor-gate pattern for deterministic concurrency tests — strongest, genuinely Muxy-derived
64	
65	Muxy tests exact concurrency behavior (caps, coalescing, "last request wins") by injecting a
66	private `actor` that holds `CheckedContinuation`s and lets the test resolve them in a chosen
67	order — no `Task.sleep`, no timing flakiness. Reference: `GitRepositoryCheckCoordinatorTests.swift:148-211`
68	(`GitRepositoryCheckProbe` — `waitForActiveChecks(_:)` suspends until N concurrent calls are
69	in-flight, `releaseAll()` releases them, test asserts `maximumActiveCheckCount == 2`). The same
70	idiom recurs independently 11 times across Muxy's suite for different subsystems.
71	
72	Workroom's equivalent today is `WorkroomAppTests/Support/Settle.swift` — a run-loop-pumping
73	poll-until-condition-or-ceiling helper (0.6s default) used by 7 files including named hang
74	regression suites. It's timing-based by construction: it works, but it proves "didn't happen
75	within N seconds," not "provably cannot happen."
76	
77	This is worth adopting specifically because Workroom already has bug history in exactly this
78	class of race: the DiffViewer `.task` re-fire loop (memory: `macapp-diffviewer-task-refire-loop.md`),
79	the History-loads-forever GCD starvation (memory: `macapp-history-loads-forever-gcd.md`), and
80	`AppStoreDeleteRaceTests`. An actor-gate test on any of these would assert the invariant
81	directly (e.g. "at most one load in flight for a given file key") instead of asserting "settled
82	within 0.6s," and would fail deterministically rather than flake under load.
83	
84	**Concrete, verified target**: `AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift:457-491` (`runLocalSweep`) and its
85	sibling `runCISweep` (:493-529) are the closest structural match to Muxy's
86	`GitRepositoryCheckCoordinator` in the whole codebase — a `cap`-bounded `withTaskGroup` fan-out
87	(refill-as-completes) over the already-injectable `WorkroomStatusResolver`. Confirmed by grep:
88	`runLocalSweep`/`runCISweep` have **zero** test coverage today (no hits in `WorkroomAppTests/`),
89	so the cap-bounded concurrency invariant ("at most `cap` local probes in flight") is currently
90	unverified by any test — exactly the class of bug an actor-gate stub proves deterministically.
91	Caveat: both methods are `private` to the `AppStore` extension, so a test would need to either go
92	through the public `refreshWorkroomStatuses`/`scheduleSelectedStatusRefresh` entry points, or the
93	methods would need to move to `internal` for direct `@testable import` access.
94	
95	### 2. `NSHostingView` + `layoutSubtreeIfNeeded()` + `fittingSize` — closes a real CI gap
96	
97	Muxy tests SwiftUI layout behavior without XCUITest and without snapshot testing: build the real
98	view via `NSHostingView(rootView:)`, force layout, assert on `fittingSize`/subview structure.
99	Reference: `ExtensionConsentDialogTests.swift:36-51`.
100	
101	The reason this matters for Workroom isn't "lighter than XCUITest" in the abstract — it's a
102	concrete CI asymmetry already on record: `.github/workflows/ci.yml:230-245` runs `make app-test`
103	but never `make app-uitest` ("UI tests don't run on GitHub CI" per project memory). Any
104	layout/structure assertion written as an `NSHostingView` unit test runs in the tier CI actually
105	executes on every push; the same assertion as an XCUITest only runs when someone remembers to
106	run it locally. This moves coverage from never-verified-on-CI to verified-on-every-push for
107	SwiftUI views that don't need a live window or real terminal content.
108	
109	Not a replacement for Workroom's XCUITest tier — Workroom's fixture/accessibility-based terminal
110	content assertions (`readText`, `GhosttySurfaceView` accessibility overrides) have no Muxy
111	equivalent at all (Muxy has zero XCUITest, by explicit "never run the app" policy) and are more
112	sophisticated than anything in Muxy. This technique is a narrow, useful addition for pure-SwiftUI
113	layout checks specifically.
114	
115	### 3. Meta-test guarding your own scripts
116	
117	Muxy has `TestIsolationScriptTests.swift:43-51` — a test that reads `scripts/checks.sh`'s source
118	as text and asserts it still invokes the test-isolation wrapper, guarding against someone
119	silently removing it. Pure string-read-and-assert, zero framework friction, trivial to port to
120	XCTest.
121	
122	Workroom has comparably fragile invariants living only in `Makefile` comments today: the
123	`APP_UITEST_FLAGS` skip list (3 UI tests skipped by default per `Makefile:60-67`), CI's
124	`make app-test-scripts` invocation, and `app-release` deliberately *not* depending on `app-test`
125	(`Makefile:116`). A small test class that greps `Makefile`/`ci.yml` for these strings would catch
126	someone accidentally dropping one during a refactor, the same way Muxy's does.
127	
128	### 4. `XCTSkip` for build-artifact-dependent tests
129	
130	Muxy's session-daemon E2E tests use `.enabled(if: SessionDaemonHarness.binaryURL != nil)` to skip
131	gracefully — rather than fail — when a debug binary they depend on hasn't been built. The direct
132	XCTest translation is `throw XCTSkip(...)` at the top of the test. Relevant if Workroom's
133	`run-supervisor` Python tests or any future test depends on a built CLI/helper binary being
134	present; worth keeping in mind rather than failing hard or silently no-op'ing.
135	
136	## Real duplication found in both — not "Muxy learnings," found while comparing
137	
138	These three gaps exist in **both** codebases. Muxy does not do them well either (see specifics
139	below), so they're not "adopt Muxy's approach" — they're independently-confirmed opportunities
140	Workroom could get right where Muxy hasn't:
141	
142	- **Shared VCS test-double module.** Workroom re-implements `VCSProviding`/`StatusCommandRunning`/
143	  `VCSWriting` stubs privately in ~10 files (`BranchResolverTests.swift:7` `StubProvider`,
144	  `HistoryModelTests.swift:18` `FakeProvider`, `WorkroomStatusResolverTests.swift:7`
145	  `MockStatusRunner`, etc.) with no shared `Fakes.swift`. Muxy has the same problem — its
146	  `Support/` folder exists but doesn't consolidate the analogous `TempGitRepo`/`StubURLProtocol`
147	  duplication (3 independent `TempGitRepo` copies, `StubURLProtocol` duplicated in 3 files, 11
148	  files with private `makeTempDir()`).
149	- **Shared git/jj repo fixture builder.** ~20 Workroom files each hand-roll `tempDir()`/
150	  `gitRepo(files:)`/`jjRepo()` (e.g. `VCSCommitIntegrationTests.swift:78-83`,
151	  `WorkroomStatusIntegrationTests.swift` separately defining `gitRepoWithUpstream()` and
152	  `jjRepo()`). Muxy's XCUITest-equivalent problem is identical in shape.
153	- **Shared XCUITest launch/wait helpers.** 33 of Workroom's 37 UI test files independently
154	  redeclare `launchedApp()`/`waitExists()`. N/A comparison to Muxy (no XCUITest there), but it's
155	  the same duplication shape as the two items above and worth fixing in the same pass if ever
156	  addressed.
157	
158	## Considered and declined
159	
160	- **Coverage gate** (Muxy: `MIN_LINE_COVERAGE=90` via `xcrun llvm-cov report`, opt-in, scoped to
161	  Models/parsers). Not recommended. Muxy's own gate visibly produced `ModelCoverageTests.swift` —
162	  a `.serialized` grab-bag suite stitching ~12 unrelated small assertions together, which the
163	  survey flags as a coverage-driven anti-pattern, not a model to import.
164	- **Global test-process detection to auto-isolate storage** (Muxy: `MuxyFileStorage.isTestProcess`
165	  redirects Application Support JSON persistence via `MUXY_TEST_APPLICATION_SUPPORT_DIRECTORY`).
166	  Investigated and rejected for Workroom specifically:
167	  - Muxy's mechanism only covers its JSON file persistence layer — it does *not* solve
168	    UserDefaults isolation globally either; Muxy still hand-rolls `UserDefaults(suiteName:
169	    "...-\(UUID())")` independently in 22 files, the same per-site pattern Workroom already has.
170	  - Workroom's actual hazard is `Defaults`-backed keys (sindresorhus/Defaults) sharing one real
171	    on-disk UserDefaults domain across parallel test workers (per-process `$HOME`/env overrides
172	    don't touch it — cfprefsd resolves the real home regardless, per memory
173	    `userdefaults-not-isolated-by-home.md`).
174	  - Workroom already made a deliberate, documented architectural call here:
175	    `WorkroomAppTests/SharedPrefDefaultsTests.swift` explains in detail why per-property
176	    `...ForTesting` override flags on `AppStore` (not blanket isolation) were chosen — ~47
177	    production call sites branch on the real fixture/prefs keys, so auto-isolating everything
178	    when a test process is detected would silently change behavior those sites depend on. The
179	    single-writer-class discipline for raw key writes, and per-property overrides for everything
180	    else, is already the considered-correct answer to the exact problem Muxy's mechanism targets.
181	  - Verified before writing this off: 282 of 389 `Defaults.Key` declarations already scope to an
182	    explicit `suite:`, and multiple existing tests (`SharedPrefDefaultsTests`, `RunCommandTests`,
183	    `ConfirmOnCloseTerminalTests`, etc.) rely on specific `ForTesting` flags being off by default.
184	    Nothing to change here.
185	
186	## Bottom line
187	
188	Three things worth doing if/when Joel wants to act on this: an actor-gate-style deterministic
189	concurrency test for one of the known race-prone subsystems (item 1), an `NSHostingView` layout
190	test for a SwiftUI view that currently only has XCUITest coverage (item 2, closes the CI gap),
191	and a small meta-test pinning the `Makefile`/CI invariants (item 3). The duplication cleanups
192	(shared fakes, shared repo builders, shared XCUITest helpers) are good chores but are
193	independent of the Muxy comparison — Muxy hasn't solved them either.
194	
195	This plan is findings-only per Joel's answer — no implementation follows from this session.

Muxy tests exact concurrency behavior (caps, coalescing, "last request wins") by injecting a
private `actor` that holds `CheckedContinuation`s and lets the test resolve them in a chosen
order — no `Task.sleep`, no timing flakiness. Reference: `GitRepositoryCheckCoordinatorTests.swift:148-211`

poll-until-condition-or-ceiling helper (0.6s default) used by 7 files including named hang
regression suites. It's timing-based by construction: it works, but it proves "didn't happen
within N seconds," not "provably cannot happen."

1	# Muxy vs Workroom test practices — findings
2	
3	## Context
4	
5	Joel asked for a review of how Muxy (`~/dev/muxy`, sibling ghostty-based Swift terminal app,
6	pulled to latest `origin/main` @ `03a6420`, 2026-08-12) implements its tests, to see what could
7	improve Workroom's macapp test suite. This is a findings-only writeup — no code changes.
8	
9	Both projects are macOS/SwiftUI apps built on libghostty with git/VCS-heavy domains, which makes
10	the comparison unusually direct. Key framework difference up front: **Muxy is 100% Swift Testing
11	(`@Test`/`#expect`, 334 files, 3,297 tests); Workroom is 100% XCTest (147 files, 2,263 tests).**
12	No Swift Testing migration is proposed — at Workroom's scale that's a non-starter, and several
13	Muxy patterns below are trait-shaped (`.serialized`, `.timeLimit`, `@Test(arguments:)`) with no
14	clean XCTest equivalent, so they're named as XCTest-form translations or dropped, not copied.
15	
16	## Adoptable patterns, ranked
17	
18	### 1. Actor-gate pattern for deterministic concurrency tests — refines, doesn't introduce, a pattern Workroom already has
19	
20	Muxy tests exact concurrency behavior (caps, coalescing, "last request wins") by injecting a
21	private `actor` that holds `CheckedContinuation`s and lets the test resolve them in a chosen
22	order — no `Task.sleep`, no timing flakiness. Reference: `GitRepositoryCheckCoordinatorTests.swift:148-211`
23	(`GitRepositoryCheckProbe` — `waitForActiveChecks(_:)` suspends until N concurrent calls are
24	in-flight, `releaseAll()` releases them, test asserts `maximumActiveCheckCount == 2`). The same
25	idiom recurs independently 11 times across Muxy's suite for different subsystems.
26	
27	**Correction from outside-voice review**: this idiom is not new to Workroom. `GatedGHRunner`
28	(`WorkroomStatusTests.swift:977`, a `StatusCommandRunning` conformer holding a
29	`CheckedContinuation<Void, Never>`) already gates a single call deterministically — the same
30	continuation-based mechanics Muxy uses. The genuinely missing piece isn't the gating idiom, it's
31	**concurrent-call accounting**: Muxy's `GitRepositoryCheckProbe` additionally counts how many
32	calls are in flight *simultaneously* and asserts a maximum (`maximumActiveCheckCount == 2`).
33	Workroom has no test today that asserts an N-in-flight invariant the way Muxy's does — that's the
34	real, narrower gap.
35	
36	Workroom's other equivalent is `WorkroomAppTests/Support/Settle.swift` — a run-loop-pumping
37	poll-until-condition-or-ceiling helper (0.6s default) used by 7 files including named hang
38	regression suites. It's timing-based by construction: it works, but it proves "didn't happen
39	within N seconds," not that it cannot happen under any schedule the test didn't try (an actor
40	gate exercises a chosen, deterministic interleaving — it narrows the flake surface, it doesn't
41	prove the invariant across every possible interleaving either).
42	
43	This is worth pursuing specifically because Workroom already has bug history in exactly this
44	class of race: the DiffViewer `.task` re-fire loop (memory: `macapp-diffviewer-task-refire-loop.md`),
45	the History-loads-forever GCD starvation (memory: `macapp-history-loads-forever-gcd.md`), and
46	`AppStoreDeleteRaceTests`.
47	
48	**On a concrete target — checked and it's blocked today.** `AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift:457-491`
49	(`runLocalSweep`) is the closest structural match to Muxy's `GitRepositoryCheckCoordinator` — a
50	`cap`-bounded `withTaskGroup` fan-out over `WorkroomStatusResolver`, with zero test coverage of
51	the cap invariant today. But unlike Muxy's coordinator, **it has no usable injection seam for the
52	git path**: `WorkroomStatusResolver.resolveGit` (`WorkroomStatusResolver.swift:94-96`) calls
53	`GitProvider().workingStatus(root:)` directly through `runBlocking`, bypassing the injectable
54	`StatusCommandRunning` runner entirely (that seam only covers the GitHub CLI/PR probes, not local
55	git/jj status reads). `resolveJJ` similarly calls into the native jj core directly. Testing
56	`runLocalSweep`'s cap deterministically would require adding a real injection point to
57	`resolveGit`/`resolveJJ` first — a production-code change, not a test-only addition, and more
58	than the "bump to internal visibility" caveat this doc originally suggested. Scope it as such if
59	picked up: **first** add a seam (protocol or closure) around the local-status probe, **then**
60	actor-gate-test the cap.
61	
62	### 2. Meta-test guarding your own scripts
63	
64	Muxy has `TestIsolationScriptTests.swift:43-51` — a test that reads `scripts/checks.sh`'s source
65	as text and asserts it still invokes the test-isolation wrapper, guarding against someone
66	silently removing it. Pure string-read-and-assert, zero framework friction.
67	
68	Workroom has comparably fragile invariants living only in `Makefile` comments today: the
69	`APP_UITEST_FLAGS` skip list (**4** UI tests skipped by default per `Makefile:67` — corrected
70	from an earlier miscount in this doc's research pass: `AgentResumeUITests`,
71	`SessionRestoreUITests`, `HistoryStressUITests/testLargeHistoryStaysInteractive`,
72	`WindowDragUITests/testDraggingWorkroomTabReordersTwoChips`), and CI's `make app-test-scripts`
73	invocation (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:245`).
74	
75	**Correction from outside-voice review**: porting this straight into an XCTest class (as
76	originally proposed here) tests spelling, not behavior — it'd still pass if the skip list became
77	unreachable, got overridden by an env var, or the guarded command moved to a different workflow
78	file entirely, and it awkwardly couples the expensive, host-app-launching `WorkroomAppTests`
79	bundle to repository layout for a check that's really "did these two files still say X." Better
80	fit: a standalone check in the existing dependency-free script tier (alongside
81	`Scripts/build-helper_test.sh`/`Scripts/channel-helper_test.sh`, run via `make app-test-scripts`)
82	rather than a new XCTest class.
83	
84	Also drop the `app-release` doesn't-depend-on-`app-test` pin from scope — it checks the wrong
85	invariant. The actual safety property is that release/nightly CI workflows run `app-test`
86	*somewhere*, separately (per `Makefile:116`'s comment on why `app-release` intentionally excludes
87	it — Debug-only single-arch builds pin a different shape than the release artifact). A test that
88	only asserts the Makefile's dependency graph excludes `app-test` could stay green while that
89	separate CI safety net silently disappeared. If this is ever built, pin the CI workflow's actual
90	test invocations, not the Makefile target graph.
91	
92	## Real duplication found in both — not "Muxy learnings," found while comparing
93	
94	These three gaps exist in **both** codebases. Muxy does not do them well either (see specifics
95	below), so they're not "adopt Muxy's approach" — they're independently-confirmed opportunities
96	Workroom could get right where Muxy hasn't:
97	
98	- **Shared VCS test-double module.** Workroom re-implements `VCSProviding`/`StatusCommandRunning`/
99	  `VCSWriting` stubs privately in ~10 files (`BranchResolverTests.swift:7` `StubProvider`,
100	  `HistoryModelTests.swift:18` `FakeProvider`, `WorkroomStatusResolverTests.swift:7`
101	  `MockStatusRunner`, etc.) with no shared `Fakes.swift`. Muxy has the same problem — its
102	  `Support/` folder exists but doesn't consolidate the analogous `TempGitRepo`/`StubURLProtocol`
103	  duplication (3 independent `TempGitRepo` copies, `StubURLProtocol` duplicated in 3 files, 11
104	  files with private `makeTempDir()`).
105	- **Shared git/jj repo fixture builder.** ~20 Workroom files each hand-roll `tempDir()`/
106	  `gitRepo(files:)`/`jjRepo()` (e.g. `VCSCommitIntegrationTests.swift:78-83`,
107	  `WorkroomStatusIntegrationTests.swift` separately defining `gitRepoWithUpstream()` and
108	  `jjRepo()`). Muxy's XCUITest-equivalent problem is identical in shape.
109	- **Shared XCUITest launch/wait helpers.** 33 of Workroom's 37 UI test files independently
110	  redeclare `launchedApp()`/`waitExists()`. N/A comparison to Muxy (no XCUITest there), but it's
111	  the same duplication shape as the two items above and worth fixing in the same pass if ever
112	  addressed.
113	
114	## Considered and declined
115	
116	- **Coverage gate** (Muxy: `MIN_LINE_COVERAGE=90` via `xcrun llvm-cov report`, opt-in, scoped to
117	  Models/parsers). Not recommended. Muxy's own gate visibly produced `ModelCoverageTests.swift` —
118	  a `.serialized` grab-bag suite stitching ~12 unrelated small assertions together, which the
119	  survey flags as a coverage-driven anti-pattern, not a model to import.
120	- **Global test-process detection to auto-isolate storage** (Muxy: `MuxyFileStorage.isTestProcess`
121	  redirects Application Support JSON persistence via `MUXY_TEST_APPLICATION_SUPPORT_DIRECTORY`).
122	  Investigated and rejected for Workroom specifically:
123	  - Muxy's mechanism only covers its JSON file persistence layer — it does *not* solve
124	    UserDefaults isolation globally either; Muxy still hand-rolls `UserDefaults(suiteName:
125	    "...-\(UUID())")` independently in 22 files, the same per-site pattern Workroom already has.
126	  - Workroom's actual hazard is `Defaults`-backed keys (sindresorhus/Defaults) sharing one real
127	    on-disk UserDefaults domain across parallel test workers (per-process `$HOME`/env overrides
128	    don't touch it — cfprefsd resolves the real home regardless, per memory
129	    `userdefaults-not-isolated-by-home.md`).
130	  - Workroom already made a deliberate, documented architectural call here:
131	    `WorkroomAppTests/SharedPrefDefaultsTests.swift` explains in detail why per-property
132	    `...ForTesting` override flags on `AppStore` (not blanket isolation) were chosen — ~47
133	    production call sites branch on the real fixture/prefs keys, so auto-isolating everything
134	    when a test process is detected would silently change behavior those sites depend on. The
135	    single-writer-class discipline for raw key writes, and per-property overrides for everything
136	    else, is already the considered-correct answer to the exact problem Muxy's mechanism targets.
137	  - Verified before writing this off: 282 of 389 `Defaults.Key` declarations already scope to an
138	    explicit `suite:`, and multiple existing tests (`SharedPrefDefaultsTests`, `RunCommandTests`,
139	    `ConfirmOnCloseTerminalTests`, etc.) rely on specific `ForTesting` flags being off by default.
140	    Nothing to change here.
141	
142	## Bottom line
143	
144	Three things worth doing if/when Joel wants to act on this: an actor-gate-style deterministic
145	concurrency test for one of the known race-prone subsystems (item 1), an `NSHostingView` layout
146	test for a SwiftUI view that currently only has XCUITest coverage (item 2, closes the CI gap),
147	and a small meta-test pinning the `Makefile`/CI invariants (item 3). The duplication cleanups
148	(shared fakes, shared repo builders, shared XCUITest helpers) are good chores but are
149	independent of the Muxy comparison — Muxy hasn't solved them either.
150	
151	This plan is findings-only per Joel's answer — no implementation follows from this session.

### `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` never reaches the `gh` auth probe (macapp) — gh-flap eng-review follow-up

**What:** decide whether `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` (or another way of resolving gh's config dir) should reach
the NON-network `run` path that `WorkroomStatusResolver.resolveGitHubCLI` uses.

**Why:** `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` *is* in `StatusCommandRunner.forwardedAuthKeys`, but that allowlist is only
applied by `networkEnvironment`, i.e. behind `if network` in `run`. The gh auth probe is a plain `run`,
and the comment justifying the split says gh "carries its own token" — true, but gh FINDS that token via
its config dir. A user who sets `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` in `.zshrc` and launches from Finder therefore hands
gh a different config root than their terminal uses. Measured: an empty gh config dir returns
`{"hosts":{}}` on stdout with exit 0, which classifies as `.notAuthenticated` — a permanent false
"GitHub CLI not signed in" for someone who is signed in everywhere else. Same false claim the
cancelled-probe fix removed, reached by a completely different route.

**Pros:** closes the last known cause of a false "not signed in". **Cons:** widening the environment on
an automatic path is a deliberate, documented narrowness (`StatusCommandRunner` explains why a
wholesale transplant is refused for anything that runs without the user asking) — this is a security
posture question, not a one-line fix. A third allowlist ("non-secret, both paths") is probably the right
shape, and `GH_CONFIG_DIR` deserves the same thought.

**How to start:** `StatusCommandRunner.run`, where `if network` selects the environment. Decide the
allowlist question first, then apply to both paths.

**Depends on:** nothing.

**Priority:** P3 — real and measured, but it needs a policy decision, and the affected configuration is
uncommon.

**What:** Add an injectable seam to `WorkroomStatusResolver.resolveGit`/`resolveJJ` (they currently call
`GitProvider().workingStatus(root:)` and the native jj core directly, bypassing the existing
`StatusCommandRunning` injection point), then write an actor-gate test on `runLocalSweep`'s (and

asserts the number of concurrent local-status probes never exceeds `cap`.

**Why:** `runLocalSweep`/`runCISweep` have zero test coverage of the cap invariant today (confirmed by
grep — no hits in `WorkroomAppTests/`). Workroom already has bug history in exactly this class of race
(the DiffViewer `.task` re-fire loop, the History-loads-forever GCD starvation), so an untested
concurrency bound here is a real, unguarded risk, not a hypothetical one. Muxy's equivalent
(`GitRepositoryCheckCoordinatorTests`) proves this class of invariant deterministically via a private
`actor` holding `CheckedContinuation`s that counts in-flight calls and asserts a max — Workroom already
has the *gating* half of that mechanic (`GatedGHRunner` in `WorkroomStatusTests.swift:977`), just not the
*counting* half.

**Context:** This was originally scoped as "just write the test" during a Muxy-vs-Workroom test-practices
comparison, then corrected during outside-voice (Codex) review: `resolveGit`/`resolveJJ` have no usable
injection seam today, so this is two steps, not one — add the seam first (a protocol or closure around
the local-status probe), then write the actor-gate test against it. Full writeup and the corrected

# Muxy vs Workroom test practices — findings

## Context

Joel asked for a review of how Muxy (`~/dev/muxy`, sibling ghostty-based Swift terminal app,
pulled to latest `origin/main` @ `03a6420`, 2026-08-12) implements its tests, to see what could
improve Workroom's macapp test suite. This is a findings-only writeup — no code changes.

Both projects are macOS/SwiftUI apps built on libghostty with git/VCS-heavy domains, which makes
the comparison unusually direct. Key framework difference up front: **Muxy is 100% Swift Testing
(`@Test`/`#expect`, 334 files, 3,297 tests); Workroom is 100% XCTest (147 files, 2,263 tests).**
No Swift Testing migration is proposed — at Workroom's scale that's a non-starter, and several
Muxy patterns below are trait-shaped (`.serialized`, `.timeLimit`, `@Test(arguments:)`) with no
clean XCTest equivalent, so they're named as XCTest-form translations or dropped, not copied.

## Adoptable patterns, ranked

### 1. Actor-gate pattern for deterministic concurrency tests — refines, doesn't introduce, a pattern Workroom already has

Muxy tests exact concurrency behavior (caps, coalescing, "last request wins") by injecting a
private `actor` that holds `CheckedContinuation`s and lets the test resolve them in a chosen
order — no `Task.sleep`, no timing flakiness. Reference: `GitRepositoryCheckCoordinatorTests.swift:148-211`
(`GitRepositoryCheckProbe` — `waitForActiveChecks(_:)` suspends until N concurrent calls are
in-flight, `releaseAll()` releases them, test asserts `maximumActiveCheckCount == 2`). The same
idiom recurs independently 11 times across Muxy's suite for different subsystems.

**Correction from outside-voice review**: this idiom is not new to Workroom. `GatedGHRunner`
(`WorkroomStatusTests.swift:977`, a `StatusCommandRunning` conformer holding a

pulled to latest `origin/main` @ `03a6420`, 2026-08-12) implements its tests, to see what could
improve Workroom's macapp test suite. This is a findings-only writeup — no code changes.

Both projects are macOS/SwiftUI apps built on libghostty with git/VCS-heavy domains, which makes
the comparison unusually direct. Key framework difference up front: **Muxy is 100% Swift Testing
(`@Test`/`#expect`, 334 files, 3,297 tests); Workroom is 100% XCTest (147 files, 2,263 tests).**
No Swift Testing migration is proposed — at Workroom's scale that's a non-starter, and several
Muxy patterns below are trait-shaped (`.serialized`, `.timeLimit`, `@Test(arguments:)`) with no
clean XCTest equivalent, so they're named as XCTest-form translations or dropped, not copied.

## Adoptable patterns, ranked

### 1. Actor-gate pattern for deterministic concurrency tests — refines, doesn't introduce, a pattern Workroom already has

Muxy tests exact concurrency behavior (caps, coalescing, "last request wins") by injecting a
private `actor` that holds `CheckedContinuation`s and lets the test resolve them in a chosen
order — no `Task.sleep`, no timing flakiness. Reference: `GitRepositoryCheckCoordinatorTests.swift:148-211`
(`GitRepositoryCheckProbe` — `waitForActiveChecks(_:)` suspends until N concurrent calls are
in-flight, `releaseAll()` releases them, test asserts `maximumActiveCheckCount == 2`). The same
idiom recurs independently 11 times across Muxy's suite for different subsystems.

**Correction from outside-voice review**: this idiom is not new to Workroom. `GatedGHRunner`
(`WorkroomStatusTests.swift:977`, a `StatusCommandRunning` conformer holding a
`CheckedContinuation<Void, Never>`) already gates a single call deterministically — the same
continuation-based mechanics Muxy uses. The genuinely missing piece isn't the gating idiom, it's
**concurrent-call accounting**: Muxy's `GitRepositoryCheckProbe` additionally counts how many
calls are in flight *simultaneously* and asserts a maximum (`maximumActiveCheckCount == 2`).
Workroom has no test today that asserts an N-in-flight invariant the way Muxy's does — that's the
real, narrower gap.

Workroom's other equivalent is `WorkroomAppTests/Support/Settle.swift` — a run-loop-pumping
poll-until-condition-or-ceiling helper (0.6s default) used by 7 files including named hang
regression suites. It's timing-based by construction: it works, but it proves "didn't happen
within N seconds," not that it cannot happen under any schedule the test didn't try (an actor
gate exercises a chosen, deterministic interleaving — it narrows the flake surface, it doesn't
prove the invariant across every possible interleaving either).

This is worth pursuing specifically because Workroom already has bug history in exactly this
class of race: the DiffViewer `.task` re-fire loop (memory: `macapp-diffviewer-task-refire-loop.md`),
the History-loads-forever GCD starvation (memory: `macapp-history-loads-forever-gcd.md`), and
`AppStoreDeleteRaceTests`.

**On a concrete target — checked and it's blocked today.** `AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift:457-491`
(`runLocalSweep`) is the closest structural match to Muxy's `GitRepositoryCheckCoordinator` — a
`cap`-bounded `withTaskGroup` fan-out over `WorkroomStatusResolver`, with zero test coverage of
the cap invariant today. But unlike Muxy's coordinator, **it has no usable injection seam for the

`StatusCommandRunning` runner entirely (that seam only covers the GitHub CLI/PR probes, not local
git/jj status reads). `resolveJJ` similarly calls into the native jj core directly. Testing
`runLocalSweep`'s cap deterministically would require adding a real injection point to
`resolveGit`/`resolveJJ` first — a production-code change, not a test-only addition, and more
than the "bump to internal visibility" caveat this doc originally suggested. Scope it as such if
picked up: **first** add a seam (protocol or closure) around the local-status probe, **then**
actor-gate-test the cap.

### 2. Meta-test guarding your own scripts

Muxy has `TestIsolationScriptTests.swift:43-51` — a test that reads `scripts/checks.sh`'s source
as text and asserts it still invokes the test-isolation wrapper, guarding against someone
silently removing it. Pure string-read-and-assert, zero framework friction.

Workroom has comparably fragile invariants living only in `Makefile` comments today: the
`APP_UITEST_FLAGS` skip list (**4** UI tests skipped by default per `Makefile:67` — corrected
from an earlier miscount in this doc's research pass: `AgentResumeUITests`,
`SessionRestoreUITests`, `HistoryStressUITests/testLargeHistoryStaysInteractive`,
`WindowDragUITests/testDraggingWorkroomTabReordersTwoChips`), and CI's `make app-test-scripts`
invocation (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:245`).

originally proposed here) tests spelling, not behavior — it'd still pass if the skip list became
unreachable, got overridden by an env var, or the guarded command moved to a different workflow
file entirely, and it awkwardly couples the expensive, host-app-launching `WorkroomAppTests`
bundle to repository layout for a check that's really "did these two files still say X." Better
fit: a standalone check in the existing dependency-free script tier (alongside

invariant. The actual safety property is that release/nightly CI workflows run `app-test`
